financials.source: Mass General Brigham FY2024 Consolidated Financial Statements; Becker's Hospital Review reporting on FY2024 results; web verification not possible in this session — figures are from public reporting in training data

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: Mass General Brigham FY2024 consolidated balance sheet — total investments including operating investments, board-designated funds, and assets whose use is limited; MGB holds one of the largest investment portfolios of any U.S. nonprofit health system
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Investment portfolio composed of operating investments (~$10B), board-designated funds (~$3B), endowment and donor-restricted funds (~$3B), and other restricted investments. MGB's investment wealth dwarfs its operating income by a factor of approximately 50x. Figures are rounded approximations from consolidated financials; exact breakdown not verified via live web access.

communityBenefit.source: MGB Community Health and Health Equity Annual Report; Massachusetts Attorney General community benefit reporting; claimed total includes unreimbursed Medicaid/Medicare, medical education, research, and community programs; charity care (financial assistance at cost) is a fraction of total claimed; exact figures not verified via live web access

taxAdvantage.notes: Mass General Brigham is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organization. With $5.6B in tax-exempt bonds outstanding, the interest subsidy is substantial. Multiple hospitals participate in 340B as DSH-eligible entities. Property tax exemption covers facilities across Massachusetts. Total estimated annual tax advantage likely exceeds $1 billion when including federal/state income tax, property tax, bond interest subsidy, and 340B savings.

layoffs.source: Becker's Hospital Review; Boston Globe; MGB announced plans to eliminate approximately 1,500 positions as part of a $250 million cost-reduction initiative following FY2023 operating losses

keyRiskFactors: Massive capital expenditure program including new facilities and expansions
Labor cost pressures and workforce shortages in competitive Boston market
Regulatory risk from Massachusetts Health Policy Commission oversight of large health systems
Concentration risk in Massachusetts market despite geographic diversification efforts

acquisitions.description: Acquired Wentworth-Douglass Hospital in Dover, New Hampshire, expanding the system's geographic footprint outside Massachusetts
acquisitions.source: MGB press release; New Hampshire health care market reports

acquisitions.description: Completed integration of Cooley Dickinson Hospital in Northampton, Massachusetts into the MGB system

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Mass General Brigham's approximately $17 billion investment portfolio is 50.7 times its $335 million operating income — among the highest ratios of any NFL-affiliated health system. This reveals a system whose balance sheet wealth vastly exceeds what it earns from actual healthcare operations.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: MGB's approximately $5.6 billion in tax-exempt bond debt is 2.55 times its $2.2 billion in claimed community benefit. However, claimed community benefit includes medical education and research that primarily serve the institution's academic mission, not direct charity care.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Massachusetts state average community benefit percentage not verified; MGB's actual charity care (financial assistance at cost) of approximately $200 million represents roughly 1% of total revenue — a fraction of the system's $17 billion investment portfolio.

accusation: Mass General Brigham holds approximately $17 billion in investments — over 50 times its $335 million operating income — while carrying $5.6 billion in tax-exempt bond debt, eliminating 1,500 positions in 2023, and compensating its CEO over $4 million, all under 501(c)(3) tax exemption as the New England Patriots' official healthcare partner.
